title: Essential surjectivity of the discrete representation to internal group functor
statement: For every topological group $G$ and carrier universe $w$, equip $\mathcal C=\mathrm{DiscreteContAction}(\mathrm{Type}(w),G)$ with a Cartesian monoidal structure and braiding. The functor $H$ of [def-exc-discrete-continuous-rep-to-commgrp] is essentially surjective: every internal commutative group object $A$ is isomorphic to $H(M)$ for some discrete continuous integer representation $M$.

proof.text: The underlying-type functor preserves finite products. A singleton with trivial action is terminal, and the carrier product with diagonal action is a binary product. The diagonal action is continuous on the discrete carrier because stabilizers are finite intersections of open stabilizers. The usual pairing of equivariant maps proves the universal property. These explicit products compare uniquely to the given Cartesian monoidal products.

Apply the product comparisons to the internal multiplication, unit and inverse of A. The internal diagrams become the commutative group identities on its carrier. Interpret the group additively and give it the canonical integer-module structure. Equivariance of multiplication and unit shows that each action map is additive, hence integer-linear; the action equations give a representation. Its stabilizers are open by continuity of the orbit maps and discreteness.

For every discrete continuous action X, equivariant functions X→A have the transported group law given by pointwise addition. Representability therefore reconstructs exactly the original unit, multiplication and inverse. Hence the identity carrier comparison is an internal group isomorphism H(M)≅A, proving essential surjectivity.
